name: Vinted
tagline: Peer-to-peer marketplace for selling and buying used clothing, with built-in payments and prepaid shipping labels.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Listing is free for sellers and buyers pay a Buyer Protection fee plus shipping, so there is no meaningful monthly number.

verdictSummary: The interface is genuinely unremarkable: a listing form, a photo grid, search filters, a chat thread. An agent can reproduce that shell in an afternoon and it will look fine. What it cannot reproduce is the tens of millions of people already browsing, the escrow that makes strangers trust each other with money, the carrier contracts that turn a sale into a scannable label, and the dispute process that decides who eats the loss when a parcel vanishes. A secondhand marketplace with one seller and no buyers is a photo album. Build the album if you want, but call it what it is.
coreLoopDIY: A local catalog of your own secondhand items with photos, prices, sizes and sold status, plus a simple public page you can link from wherever the actual buyers already are.
requirements: local image storage or an S3-compatible bucket
somewhere to host the public page if you want strangers to see it
whatYouLose: Buyers · all of them, which is the entire product
Escrow and Buyer Protection, so you are now personally handling payment disputes
Prepaid discounted carrier labels and parcel tracking baked into the sale
In-app messaging, ratings and the reputation history that makes a stranger click buy
Fraud and chargeback handling, plus the moderation that keeps counterfeits off the feed
moatNotes: Logistics is the visible hard part, but the real wall is two-sided: sellers show up because buyers are there, and buyers show up because the inventory is huge and cheap. Payments and labels are things you could in principle contract for. Demand is not.
whyPeopleStillPay: Sellers do not pay Vinted a subscription, which is exactly why the comparison breaks down: they are paying in attention and in the Buyer Protection fee their buyer absorbs, and what they get back is an audience that already wants what is in their wardrobe. The value was never the listing form. It is that you can photograph a jacket on a Sunday and have it viewed a few hundred times by Monday, get paid without trusting anyone, and drop a labelled parcel at a pickup point. Replicating that alone means finding buyers, holding funds, and negotiating carrier rates, which is three businesses, not one app.
notes: The listing UI is a one-sitting build; the demand is not. The moat is marketplace liquidity plus the payment escrow and carrier deals that let two strangers transact without either one trusting the other.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted "closet catalog" for tracking and showcasing secondhand items I am selling. This is deliberately NOT a marketplace: no buyers, no payments, no shipping integrations.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15 with the App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind.
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/closet.db, schema created on first run.
- Image uploads written to ./data/uploads and served through a route handler. No cloud storage, no external APIs.
- Single-user. One password read from ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env, checked in middleware, stored in an httpOnly signed cookie. No accounts, no OAuth, no telemetry.

Data model:
- item: id, title, description, brand, category, size, condition (new_with_tags, very_good, good, satisfactory), color, askingPrice, currency, boughtFor (nullable), status (draft, listed, reserved, sold, donated), listedOn, soldOn, soldFor, soldVia (free text, e.g. which platform), notes, createdAt.
- photo: id, itemId, filename, sortOrder.
- tag and item_tag, many to many.

Admin side (password protected):
- Item list with search over title and brand, filters for status, category and size, sort by newest or price.
- Create and edit form with multi-photo upload, drag to reorder photos, client side resize to max 1600px before upload.
- One-click status changes, and a sold dialog that captures soldFor, soldVia and soldOn.
- A "copy listing text" button that renders title, condition, size, brand, description and price as a plain text block to paste into whatever platform actually has buyers.
- Stats page: total items by status, gross sold, total boughtFor on sold items, simple realised margin, median days from listedOn to soldOn.

Public side (no auth):
- /shop: grid of items with status listed or reserved only, first photo, title, size, price.
- /shop/[id]: photo gallery, full details, and a mailto link using CONTACT_EMAIL from .env. No cart, no checkout, no messaging.

Also ship: seed script with 12 fake items, a CSV export of all items, README with setup steps and a .env.example containing ADMIN_PASSWORD and CONTACT_EMAIL.

Explicitly out of scope: payments, escrow, shipping labels, tracking, buyer accounts, reviews, chat, and any cross-posting automation. Do not stub these; leave them out.
